evidence.value: HTTP is not redirected to HTTPS

matches.why_it_matters: Credentials, cookies and session tokens must not be exposed through clear-text HTTP or downgrade paths.
matches.next_review: Confirm HTTPS is enforced for every entry point and that HTTP redirects safely before authentication or session exchange.

matches.title: Cookie security attributes
matches.why_it_matters: Cookie flags constrain session token exposure across insecure transport, browser scripts and cross-site requests.
matches.next_review: Confirm session cookies use Secure, HttpOnly and a deliberate SameSite value based on the application flow.

matches.title: Browser security mechanism headers
matches.why_it_matters: Security headers provide browser-enforced defense in depth against content injection, clickjacking and data leakage.
matches.next_review: Review CSP, frame-ancestors/X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy per route.

matches.title: Technology and version disclosure
matches.why_it_matters: Technology signals help focus later manual review and can expose unnecessary version details.
matches.next_review: Keep useful technology evidence, then remove precise version disclosure where it is not operationally required.

matches.title: Public metadata files and declared paths
matches.why_it_matters: robots.txt, sitemap.xml and well-known files can reveal intended routes, policies, identity metadata and hidden paths.
matches.next_review: Review discovered metadata paths manually and decide what belongs in scope before following sensitive paths.

matches.title: Application entry point inventory

evidence.label: state_changing
evidence.location: DELETE, GET, OPTIONS, POST, PUT, TRACE

matches.why_it_matters: A useful audit starts with a reliable inventory of URLs, forms, methods and parameters before any validation testing.
matches.next_review: Prioritize state-changing endpoints, sensitive parameters and authenticated flows for later authorized testing.

frameworks.title: Only intended user-facing endpoints are exposed

matches.title: Client-side JavaScript exposed routes
matches.why_it_matters: Client-side JavaScript often exposes API routes, identity flows and external integrations that are not visible as links.
matches.next_review: Review JavaScript-discovered endpoints before selecting any later validation or attack simulation.

frameworks.title: Review web page content for information leakage

matches.title: Authentication and account-management surface
matches.why_it_matters: Authentication, account and recovery flows usually define the highest-value manual review paths.
matches.next_review: Document every authentication path, recovery path and callback before testing controls in a later authorized phase.

matches.title: Administrative and privileged route inventory
matches.why_it_matters: Administrative routes are high-value review targets even when they are only passively discovered.
matches.next_review: Confirm ownership, required roles and whether the route should remain in scope before any access-control testing.

frameworks.title: Enumerate infrastructure and application admin interfaces

matches.title: File upload route inventory
matches.why_it_matters: Upload endpoints commonly require extra validation, storage and authorization review.
matches.next_review: Confirm accepted file types, size limits, storage location and authorization before any upload testing.

frameworks.title: Accepted files have safe size limits

matches.title: Infrastructure surface from DNS and TCP checks
matches.why_it_matters: Resolved hosts and open TCP ports help identify what infrastructure should be confirmed in or out of scope.
matches.next_review: Confirm every resolved host and open port with the application owner before expanding testing beyond the main URL.

matches.title: External and out-of-scope references
matches.why_it_matters: External references may be legitimate dependencies, third parties or missing scope items; they should not be scanned automatically.
matches.next_review: Classify each external host as third-party, dependency, redirect target or candidate scope extension.
